required_audit_coverage.name: required_audit_coverage
required_audit_coverage.detail: report covers all 42 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Was `project_state/decision_packet.md` treated as the only task authority?
Was `project_state/task_packet.json` treated as background only?
Did `decision_meta` remain valid, `APPROVED`, and aligned with active `reverse-agent-iteration@v2`?
Was the previous state governance bundle treated as accepted-with-limitations baseline?
Did this round remain one mainline, `project_governance`, while containing a fix lane and engineering lane?
Were existing state governance, retention, cleanup-plan, archive-index, manifest, context, and workstream capabilities inspected before adding code?
Did the implementation avoid duplicating command-plan, execution-log, report-summary, final-check, closeout, state manifest, context packet, and workstream registry?
Was `project_state/gates/status_policy_reconcile_result.json` generated?
Does status-policy reconcile distinguish current governance evidence from historical sample backlog?
Does status-policy reconcile prevent historical sample backlog from downgrading a non-sample governance round when active evidence passes?
Was `project_state/gates/doctor_backlog_split_result.json` generated?
Does doctor/backlog split record historical sample gaps as backlog notices rather than current blockers?
Was `project_state/gates/governance_fix_result.json` generated?
Does governance fix result show whether the previous limitation is resolved for current non-sample governance evidence?
Was `project_state/gates/cleanup_apply_safety_plan.json` generated?
Was `project_state/gates/cleanup_apply_dry_run.json` generated?
Does cleanup-apply dry run explicitly set `real_cleanup_apply=false`?
Does cleanup-apply dry run leave `deleted_files`, `moved_files`, `archived_files`, `compacted_archives`, `written_tombstones`, and `real_deletion_manifests` empty?
Was `project_state/gates/cleanup_apply_safety_result.json` generated?
Was `project_state/gates/cleanup_apply_safety_snapshot.json` generated?

Does cleanup-apply safety gate prove no real cleanup apply, deletion, move, archive, compaction, tombstone write, database, runner dispatch, model API, external tool, CI dispatch, Web runtime, or real sample processing occurred?
Was `project_state/gates/deletion_manifest_validation_result.json` generated?
Was `project_state/gates/tombstone_validation_result.json` generated?
Do manifest/tombstone validation artifacts validate schema-only or dry-run-only payloads, not real deletion payloads?
Was `project_state/gates/rollback_handoff_plan.json` generated?
Was `project_state/gates/audit_handoff_for_cleanup_apply.json` generated?
Do rollback/audit handoff artifacts state that future cleanup-apply needs a separate decision and audit?
Were `state_manifest`, `current_context_packet`, and `workstreams` refreshed for this round?
Does `workstreams.json` mark only `governance_fix_cleanup_apply_safety` as `ACTIVE_ROUND`?
Does `workstreams.json` keep real cleanup-apply deferred until a future decision?
Did command-plan authorize every executed command?
Were command-plan omitted commands left unexecuted?
Did pytest_result record real commands and exit codes?
Did focused tests cover status-policy reconciliation, doctor/backlog split, cleanup-apply safety, dry-run no-op behavior, manifest validation, and tombstone validation?
Did existing governance/gate/report tests continue to pass?
Did final-check pass cleanly, or if not, did it identify only nonblocking historical sample backlog with a clear reason?
Did report-summary synthesis pass and match the execution report?
Did run-closeout pass if authorized?
Were forbidden paths untouched?
Were `.github/workflows/*`, `.codex-skills/*`, `solve_reports/*`, `project_state/archives/*`, and `project_state/deletions/*` untouched?
Did the final report avoid any concrete sample solve/static/runtime/audit validation claim?
Did the final report explicitly state that cleanup-apply safety is dry-run-only and no real deletion occurred?
